requirements.summary: The namespace and file-content digests were identical before the repair, immediately afterward, and after restart; entry and regular-file counts also remained three and two respectively.

requirements.requirement: Make the existing inventory tree owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: The inventorysvc system identity was created, and direct final inspection after restart showed every directory and file owned by inventorysvc.

requirements.requirement: Make the inventory data readable by inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: The tree has inventory-readers group ownership with directories mode 0750 and files mode 0640. Effective-identity tests demonstrated read-only group access both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Make /srv/inventory inaccessible to users outside the authorized owner and reader group.
requirements.summary: No permissions were granted to others, and direct tests using an unrelated identity showed that it could neither traverse nor enumerate the inventory tree before or after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using an implementation compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were unchanged across execution and restart. The repair used existing native account and permission utilities, with no package installation or upgrade command present; package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre-change, post-change, behavioral, and post-restart evidence. The inventory contents were preserved, ownership and access controls are correct and persistent, and the operating-system release and kernel remained unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol was fully demonstrated and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Creating the service user/group and changing ownership and modes were necessary repair actions; the scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart-evidence protocol and its transient unit was confirmed cleaned up. The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledgement, observed disconnect, changed post-restart boot ID, and recovered data, permissions, services, security controls, and package health. Lifecycle snapshots show no failed services, unexpected listeners, package damage, or executor-created temporary residue.
